title: Haircuts for a Job Interview
hero_alt: Two people shaking hands across a desk in a bright office
card_text: Clean, conservative and settled in by the day. When to book before an interview, three safe cuts, and the beard question.
lede: For a job interview, get a clean, conservative cut a few days before, not the morning of. By interview day the edges have settled in and the cut looks like your hair, just at its neatest. Stick to a style you already know how to wear, keep the neckline and sideburns tidy, and decide what the beard is doing well ahead of time.
Here's how to time it, three cuts that read well in almost any interview room, and what to book.

blocks.heading: A few days before.
paragraphs: A cut done the same morning can look just a little too fresh: pale skin where the fade was, a line-up so sharp it draws the eye. Give it a few days and it reads as you on a good day, which is the goal.
Don't try something new right before an interview. If a style is new to you, you won't know how it behaves on a rushed morning. Save a big change for after you've got the job, or do it weeks ahead.
Interviews come up on short notice. If yours is this week, text me and ask what's open. Booksy shows the next available times too.

blocks.heading: Neat beats trendy.
bullets: A clean neckline above the collar. All three haircut services end with a straight razor there.
Even sideburns, trimmed to a tidy bottom edge.
Nothing over the eyes. If your fringe falls forward, plan how you'll keep it out of your face.
A beard that looks intentional, whatever its length.
A style you can recreate yourself on the day, without help.

subsections.heading: Low taper
paragraphs: Edges cleaned up low around the ears and at the nape, with length left on the sides. Tidy from every angle and quiet enough for any room, from an office to a site trailer.

subsections.heading: Hard part
paragraphs: A side part with a line shaved in where your hair naturally divides. It looks deliberate and polished. If you're unsure how a strong line will go over, ask for a softer part instead.

subsections.heading: Slick back
paragraphs: A longer top combed back over a taper, like the cut in the photo. Classic with a suit or a collared shirt. Practice the styling before the day so it holds through the whole interview.

blocks.heading: Trimmed, or gone.
paragraphs: Keeping it? The Signature Cut ({{price:signature-cut}}, {{minutes:signature-cut}}) trims or lines up the beard and finishes with a hot towel and razor detailing, so the face matches the haircut.

Taking it off? The Straight Razor Beard Shave ({{price:straight-razor-beard-shave}}, {{minutes:straight-razor-beard-shave}}) is a traditional wet shave with hot towels. If you've had a beard for years, shave it a few days before the interview rather than the night before, so your face has time to look normal to you.
No beard at all? The Essential Haircut ({{price:essential-haircut}}, {{minutes:essential-haircut}}) is the cut, the neck cleanup and a finished style.

blocks.heading: The morning of.
blocks.lead: Give the styling a few extra minutes.
paragraphs: Style your hair the way you practiced, then check the back and sides in a second mirror. The parts of a cut you can't see are the parts an interviewer sits behind or beside.
Skip the cap or hat on the drive over. A dent across the top is hard to fix in the car five minutes before you go in.
Run a hand down your collar before you head inside. Loose clippings and a crooked collar are the only things a fresh neckline can't fix.

items.q: How many days before an interview should I get a haircut?
items.a: A few days before. The cut has time to settle, and it still looks neat on the day.

items.q: What haircut is good for a job interview?
items.a: A clean, conservative one you already know how to style: a low taper, a side part with a hard part, or a slick back.

items.q: Should I shave my beard for an interview?
items.a: Not necessarily. A neatly trimmed beard looks intentional. If you do shave it, do it a few days ahead.

items.q: Is a fade OK for an interview?
items.a: Yes, as long as it's clean. A low fade or a low taper is the quieter choice if you're unsure about the workplace.

tim_questions: Confirm the 'a few days before' timing for interview cuts (the plan suggested 3-5 days).
